title: Interdisciplinary Teams for Teacher Professional Development
extended_summary:
This paper describes the design and iterative refinement of SATTAA, the San Antonio Teacher Training Astronomy Academy, a teacher professional development program intended to strengthen secondary teachers’ astronomy content knowledge, pedagogical approaches, and comfort teaching STEM. The authors frame the problem as a persistent lack of astronomy background among secondary teachers, alongside a need to connect disciplinary content with hands-on pedagogy and technology in ways that support more confident instruction and greater student interest in STEM.

The intervention is an interdisciplinary, team-designed summer professional development program that evolved across three annual iterations (2018–2020). The program was developed and delivered by astronomers, STEM educators, and informal education partners, with formats shifting from mostly face-to-face to blended and then fully online during COVID-19. Participants were preservice and inservice teachers from the San Antonio area; the 2018 pilot involved preservice teachers only, 2019 added inservice teachers, and 2020 expanded participation further and included more online components and virtual field experiences.

Evidence reported in the paper comes from participant surveys, pre/post content quizzes, reflections, focus groups, and team observations used to guide redesign. Across iterations, participants consistently reported improved astronomy understanding, greater interest, and appreciation for the interdisciplinary and collaborative structure. The authors conclude that combining disciplinary expertise with pedagogy and informal education partnerships improved the quality and adaptability of teacher professional development, though they note that the paper mainly reports processes and lessons learned rather than a controlled evaluation of outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system is an adaptive educational software system that provides instructional support, practice, and feedback tailored to learners.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper does not evaluate an AI tool. It describes a teacher professional development program (SATTAA) and its interdisciplinary design, with astronomy content, pedagogy, and technology integration; any technology mentioned is general online meeting and field-trip tooling rather than an AI system.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive program paper about teacher professional development design and iteration, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. No AI system is studied, and no causal evidence about an AI product is presented.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no AI intervention and no tool-level outcome to assess. The reported gains relate to teacher content knowledge within a PD program, not to AI-mediated coaching or lesson-plan feedback.
